title: Glessner's stable roof: the 1887 photograph's camera was wrong, not the roof
items: Nothing you can see changes. An 1887 photograph seemed to show the stable's roof a third longer than a 1963 one, because it was being read through a camera fitted to the alley wall. Read through the camera fitted at the stable, its tiles come out at the 5 inches the 1963 surveyors measured.
Both photographs show the alley end of that roof a few feet shorter from eave to ridge than the model draws it. That is now its own ticket, to rebuild the roof or explain the difference.
